_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for BKR retrospectives (retro/build_bkr.py): Baker Hughes Incorporated, listed on the NYSE as BHI throughout 2007-2009 (BKR is the series key). Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date. A filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day ('filed' keeps the acceptance time, US Eastern; EDGAR gives only the filing date before 2003); the earnings 8-Ks of 2007-2009 were accepted before the open on their release days. The builder uses the latest history vintage published by AS_OF, the prints published by AS_OF that report a fiscal year after that history (a Q4 print reports the year just ended and extends the history until the 10-K), and the latest declared dividend. Fiscal years are calendar years from 1998 (fiscal 1997 ended September 30). Baker Hughes gives no EPS, total-revenue or margin guidance in numbers in any filing of 2007-2009: each release's Outlook section guides revenue outside North America (in words or as a range), corporate expenses, capital expenditures, depreciation and the tax rate, kept on the print as 'outlook' (display only), and the 2009 releases have no Outlook section. Values are as reported; a vintage takes each year from the latest filing that reports it, and the company's operating profit per diluted share replaces GAAP EPS where a filing publishes it (the history's 'normalization' says which). A print's growth rates and margins are derived from the raw figures of its release ('raw'; the builder re-derives and checks them): the year-ago quarter is the one the same release shows. Outside North America is the release's Oilfield Operations revenue less North America. rule_t holds the annual values behind the engine's signal thresholds. Edit only to add newly published facts or fix a transcription error against the cited filing.

history_vintages.why: Baker Hughes: 'We are a leading provider of drilling, formation evaluation, completion and production products and services to the worldwide oil and natural gas industry'; 'The primary driver of our business is our customers’ capital and operating expenditures dedicated to exploring, and drilling for, and developing and producing oil and natural gas'; 'Our business is cyclical and is dependent upon our customers’ forecasts of future oil and natural gas prices, future economic growth and hydrocarbon demand and estimates of future oil and natural gas production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed' (its own FY2006 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' drilling and production spending through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; no disruption theme is live for an oilfield services company
history_vintages.eps_excluded_note: 1998 is excluded: a loss from continuing operations of $(0.92) per diluted share (FY2002 10-K, the latest filing that reports it; the Western Atlas merger costs, an unusual charge and other charges of that year), with no published figure excluding its charges (the r2 rule for a loss year), so the EPS history, the revenue and share histories and the P/E window start with 1999 (the ACN FY02 and AAPL FY2002 rule); fiscal 1997 (the year to September 30, 1997) lies before it

rule_t._doc: Rule T values behind the engine's signal thresholds (retro/README.md, 'BKR'): the decade of the FY2006 10-K, the vintage public on 2008-01-04, is fiscal 1997-2006, ten year-on-year changes. Fiscal 1997 ended September 30, 1997 and fiscal 1998 is calendar 1998 (the company moved its year end to December 31 from 1998; the three-month transition period of October-December 1997 is not a fiscal year), so the 1998 change compares calendar 1998 with the year to September 1997, as the filings place them side by side. Each change comes from the latest 10-K published by 2008-01-04 that reports both years; seams stay as published (the Process segment shown as discontinued in the FY1999 10-K and restored in the FY2000 10-K, later discontinued businesses, the Western Atlas pooling). North America is the United States plus Canada in each 10-K's table of revenues by country (the releases' North America is 'United States and Canada'); outside North America is the rest. 'raw' keeps each change's two years as published.

na_rev.sources: revenues by country, United States plus Canada: BK1 (fiscal 1997), BK2 (1998), BK3 (1999), BK4 (2000), BK5 (2001), BK6 (2002), BK8 (2003), BK10 (2004), BK12 (2005-2006)

intl_rev.sources: total revenues less United States and Canada, the same tables: BK1 (fiscal 1997), BK2 (1998), BK3 (1999), BK4 (2000), BK5 (2001), BK6 (2002), BK8 (2003), BK10 (2004), BK12 (2005-2006)

gross_margin.sources: revenues less cost of revenues (research and engineering included, as each 10-K's selected data shows it; the FY2006 10-K's 'cost of revenues and research and engineering'), the same tables as revenue

op_margin.sources: operating income on revenues, the same tables as revenue (as published, the 1998 merger costs and unusual charge and fiscal 1997's acquired in-process research and development included)
